note: Conflicts between sources, or between a source and the published corpus, that need research or an expert ruling before they can be resolved. See README.md for the format. `sync_source_conflicts` materialises the affected rows as ReviewNote records so each conflict reaches the editorial queue rather than living only in this file.

conflicts.title: Hannan records class 9 nouns with class 6 plurals; Fortune does not list class 9 among class 6's correlating singulars
conflicts.summary: Fortune Vol 1 3.3.9 (printed p.52) states class 6 nouns 'are correlative plurals of nouns in cll. 5, 11, 21, 1a, 1 and 14' and enumerates them; class 9 is absent from that list. Hannan records class 9 nouns whose plural prefix is ma-, a class 6 shape.

sources.claim: budiriro n 9, pl: mab- -- a class 9 noun with a class 6 plural
sources.verbatim: budiriro [HHHL]KMZ n 9, pl: mab-, Success. 2. Progress (cultural).

evidence: The scan was read directly with tools/render_dictionary_entry.py; this is not an extraction artefact.
Several other class 9 rows in the audit work list carry mab-/mabv-/mabw- shapes, so this is likely a group rather than one entry.
conflicts.resolution_needed: The attested surface now publishes under the register policy (Hannan holds authority for noun class data, Fortune for concord rules), so no record is withheld. What remains open is the classification: whether Hannan's class 9 should map to a class 6 plural in the NounClass table, or Fortune's correlation list governs. Needs a source that states class 9's plural behaviour or a Shona grammarian's ruling.
conflicts.impact: 9 records publish the attested plural with the classification flagged; no data withheld

conflicts.title: Hannan's class 2b label does not match Fortune's class 2b definition
conflicts.summary: Hannan labels the amai/ambuya-type nouns 'n 2b'. Fortune Vol 1 3.3.5 defines class 2b as the prefix /a-/ occurring with two stems only (amai, ambuya) and gives no plural. There is no NounClass row for 2b, so those records carry no class at all.

sources.claim: class 2b is /a-/, occurring with the two stems mai and mbuya
amai, amaiguru, ambuya and relatives are labelled n 2b

evidence: Nine published records carry the parser's class value '2b' with no NounClass row to resolve to.
Their plurals are recorded as full forms (madzimai, vadzimbuya), so the plural itself is attested and publishes; only the class is unresolved.
conflicts.resolution_needed: Decide whether to add NounClass rows for Hannan's sub-labels (2b, 2m) with a concord taken from a source, or to remap them to an existing class. Adding a row requires an evidence-backed concord; the number of affected records is small (10).
conflicts.impact: 10 published records with no noun class

conflicts.title: The dictionary text extraction contains Cyrillic homoglyphs
conflicts.field: source quality (all fields read from the text)
conflicts.summary: local_source_cache/hannan_dictionary.txt contains 1,313 Cyrillic lookalike characters (U+0430 а, U+0442 т, U+041C М and others) where Latin letters belong. Any value read from that file could carry them into a published surface form.

sources.claim: e.g. map- appears as mаp- with U+0430

evidence: Counted by scanning the file for the Cyrillic block: 1,313 characters.
Reading from the text was introduced for plural prefixes at the same time as the normaliser, so no homoglyph has reached a published form.
conflicts.resolution_needed: None for the plural path, which normalises before use. Worth re-running the extraction or normalising at ingest if the text is ever used for other fields; an unresolved homoglyph is invisible in review.
conflicts.impact: none on published data; a latent hazard for any future consumer of that file

conflicts.title: Two published headwords are sourced to one printed line, and the page prints only one of them
conflicts.summary: The lemmas `bimha` and `bimba` both cite hannan:page_021:entry_007, but the printed line reads `bimba [LL] KMZ n 5, pl: map-, mab- (M), Reedbuck R 292.` The string `bimha` occurs nowhere on that page, so one of the two headwords was not extracted from print.

sources.verbatim: bimba [LL] KMZ n 5, pl: map-, mab- (M), Reedbuck R 292.

sources.claim: one line produced two lemma headwords

evidence: Found by the tone audit: the headword could not be rendered because it has no text hit on the page it cites.
A vision query on the crop independently spelled b-i-m-b-a and quoted [LL].
Both lemmas carry the same tone (LL), so the tone verdict for the line is unaffected either way.
conflicts.resolution_needed: Determine which headword is spurious. If `bimha` is not in the scan, the record is a parser artefact and should be retired; if it is a homograph printed elsewhere, its source locator is wrong. Needs a scan check across the dictionary for both spellings before acting.
conflicts.impact: two published lemmas from one printed entry; related to the 3,519 duplicate normalized-headword groups already known, which this gives a first concrete cause for

conflicts.title: Headwords diverge from the scan: a consonant read as a neighbour, and a tone diacritic that is not printed
conflicts.summary: Three of nine headwords on Hannan page 500 differ from the scan. Two are the same consonant-neighbour misread as the plural prefixes (`nzvinzvi-i` -> `nzvinzi-i`, dropping the v; `nzwaivhi` -> `nzwaiwhi`, v read as w). The third adds a tone diacritic the page does not print (`nzvirihi` -> `nzvirihì`), which is more dangerous: it looks like data rather than damage.

sources.verbatim: nzvinzvi-i [HL] KMZ ideo of Being pitch-black. / nzvirihi [LLH]M n 9 Mozambique Canary R859. / nzwaivhi [LHL]Z n 10 Chameleons (pl of rwaivhi).

sources.claim: the corpus holds nzvinzi-i, nzvirihì, nzwaiwhi

evidence: Found by the per-field audit on 2026-09-16; the three audited fields (tone, POS, class) were clean on the same page, so this is not a reading error in the audit.
Read at 8x and 12x and through an independent vision query, which agreed.
conflicts.resolution_needed: Measure the field before repairing it: a scan check of headwords across the dictionary is needed to size the consonant and diacritic misread classes, since a repair needs to know whether it is correcting three records or three hundred. Both classes are mechanical to detect.
conflicts.impact: 3 of 9 headwords on one page; the field has never been audited at scale, and a wrong headword is the most visible defect a dictionary can have

conflicts.title: Multi-word ideophones publish only the first word's tone pattern
conflicts.summary: A two-word ideophone headword carries one tone group per word (`kwakwara kwakwara [LLL LLL]`), and some entries publish only the first group (`LLL`). Four of the forty entries audited on Hannan page 300 do this, so the loss is real but NOT universal: `badara badara` publishes `LLL LLL` correctly, and `bha bha bha` publishes `H H H`.

sources.locator: dictionary p.300, PDF p.324, entries 1, 3, 7 and others
sources.claim: the bracket prints a pattern per word
sources.verbatim: kwakwara kwakwara [LLL LLL]Z ideo of Making a noise (as of sticks).

sources.claim: only the first group is stored

evidence: Found by the per-field audit on 2026-09-16 over all 40 entries of the page, every crop re-read independently.
Not a missing capability: the engine already stores a multi-word bracket correctly elsewhere (`munhondo churu` -> LLL HH), so the loss is in the ideophone path.

Measured after the audit: 1,174 of the 6,272 ideophone lemmas have a multi-word headword, and the published shapes differ between them -- some keep one group per word, some keep only the first, some join the groups without a space (`bambai bambai` -> `LLHLLH`).
conflicts.resolution_needed: Size it before repairing it: for the 1,174 multi-word ideophones, compare the stored pattern with the scan's bracket. A repair needs to know whether it is correcting four records or four hundred, and the same audit will show whether the joined spelling (`LLHLLH`) is a different defect or the same pattern written without a space. The non-ideophone records already answer the modelling question -- `munhondo churu` stores `LLL HH` -- so the target shape is one pattern with the groups separated.
conflicts.impact: 4 of 40 entries on one ideophone-heavy page; 1,174 multi-word ideophones carry the shape, and the published forms differ among them
